title: Liquidity Risk
description: Run pyvar's 40 liquidity-risk functions on the live pyvar.com API: LCR and NSFR, HQLA classification, cash-flow ladders, stress scenarios, survival horizon, intraday liquidity, funding concentration and liquidity VaR. Use when the user wants liquidity ratios or stress results computed rather than only explained. Needs a free pyvar API key; the skill explains how to get one.
tagline: Liquidity-risk calculations: regulatory ratios (LCR/NSFR), HQLA, cash-flow ladders, stress scenarios, survival horizon, intraday and funding metrics. Pick the function in **Functions** below; the **Worked examples** show the request shape.

examples.title: LCR and NSFR against the 100% minimum
examples.intro: Any one currency unit throughout. LCR is HQLA over net outflows over 30 days (inflows capped at 75% of outflows); NSFR is available over required stable funding. Both are compliant at 1.0 or above.

examples.title: Survival horizon under a stressed outflow path
examples.intro: How many full days the liquidity buffer lasts when net outflows accelerate. The horizon is the last day on which the cumulative net outflow is still covered.

groups.title: Intraday Liquidity
groups.intro:
(Moved out of the LCR/NSFR group above — these are BCBS 248 intraday
monitoring functions, not LCR/NSFR calculations.)

notes.liquidity_coverage_ratio_lcr: outflows are floored so recognised inflows can offset at most 75% of gross outflows (BCBS 238 §69, the default `inflow_cap`). compliant = (LCR >= 1.0).
notes.intraday_liquidity_monitor: negative cumulative position — BCBS 248's actual "daily maximum intraday liquidity usage" tool) AND `max_usage` (drop below opening balance). Only `net_debit_peak` is the genuine BCBS 248 figure — `max_usage` is an internal metric and the two diverge whenever the balance path never actually goes negative.
notes.intraday_liquidity_stress_test: delays a fraction of inflows (`delay_factor`); an internal stress design, not a specific BCBS 248 prescribed scenario.
notes.hqla_level_2b_asset_classifier:
regulatory minimum haircut (BCBS 238 §54); pass haircut=0.50 for the lower-grade-corporate/equity sub-bucket

**Composition caps are not enforced by any function.** BCBS 238 §46-§47 caps
Level 2 assets at <= 40% of total HQLA and Level 2B at <= 15% of total HQLA.
These thresholds exist as constants in `engine/liquidity_ratios.py` but no
function combines the three classifiers' output and checks them — callers
must sum the three `post_haircut_value` results themselves and apply the
40%/15% checks.
notes.combined_stress_scenario: Combined Stress Scenario. NOT the Basel/EBA reference combined scenario: BCBS 238's own version runs off the LCR's regulator-set 3%/5%/10% retail run-off categories, not this function's flat 15% default (`retail_runoff`), which is an internal convention. The "combined deficit never better than market-wide alone" ordering property still holds regardless.
